summary.intent: Run the GSD manager command center to discuss, plan, and execute phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) — three UAT gap-closure phases for the CipherBox project milestone.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 fully completed: 8 plans executed across 3 waves with worktree isolation, code reviewed, verified against live DB, and marked complete. Phase 43 planned and 2 of 4 plans executed (43-01 durable write journal, 43-02 FUSE callback wiring) before transcript end. Phase 44 discussed and context written; planning and execution still pending.

repo: Kubo v0.40 runs with the `server` profile (not private) and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (TCP+UDP) in staging — it participates in the public DHT and broadcasts provider records for every pinned CID, making all CIDs discoverable by crawlers even though blobs are encrypted.
The `/ipfs/unpin` endpoint was protected by JwtAuthGuard only (no ownership check); signup is open via Web3Auth, so any account holder could unpin another user's content by supplying a harvested CID.

writable-share save path (`shared-write.ts:450`) drops `prunedCids` without calling unpin — there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path in the codebase, making the missing ownership check a clean security gap.
BYO IPFS provider semantics: server-side 'not pinned' errors should be swallowed; BYO advisory `pinned_cids` rows count equally in refcount logic.

`pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test -- --testPathPattern=X` is broken — pnpm inserts an extra `--` causing jest to treat the flag as a positional regex. Use `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api exec jest --testPathPattern='X'` instead.
1Password SSH commit signing requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on every git commit tool call; signing failures require restarting the 1Password app.
The gsd commit helper (`gsd_run query commit`) returns `'committed': false` as a false negative even when the commit landed — always verify with `git log`, never blind-retry.

The `worktree.cleanup-wave` helper is not idempotent: it aborts the entire run on the first blocked/already-merged entry. On retry, write a reduced manifest containing only remaining unmerged entries.
`cleanup-wave` resolves `repoRoot` from its `cwd`, so it must be run from the repository root — running it from inside an agent worktree produces false `base_mismatch` errors.

No `.prettierignore` existed in the repo, causing prettier to mangle `.planning/` docs (breaking regex pipes into table columns in VALIDATION.md). Created `.prettierignore` ignoring `.planning/`, `.claude/agents/gsd-*.md`, `.claude/commands/gsd/`, `.claude/gsd-core/`, etc.
`openapi.json` accumulates formatting-only drift as a side-effect of `nest build` — restore with `git checkout --` before merging worktrees to avoid false conflicts.

When multiple agents concurrently unpin the same deduped CID, both transactions can see stale refcounts (not-yet-committed deletes from the other). This race requires a per-CID Postgres advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid))`) — a drift-report job would detect but not fix this.

Phase 43 FUSE write durability: `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` produces 0 unit tests by design — the crate's correctness is validated by build success and integration; `cargo test -p cipherbox-sdk` is the targeted gate for Rust changes.

Phase 43: `vault.module.ts` pattern of providing `IPFS_PROVIDER` locally via `useFactory` (rather than importing `IpfsModule`) is the established way to break circular NestJS module dependencies in this repo.

code.finding: The unpin handler never read `req.user` before this phase — it passed the raw CID string directly to Kubo `pin/rm`. Post-phase-42 it delegates to `vaultService.guardedUnpin(req.user.id, dto.cid)` and returns opaque `{ success: true }` for all outcomes.

Kubo v0.40 configured with `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (TCP+UDP). The `server` profile only disables local-network discovery — full public DHT participation remains, broadcasting provider records for all pinned CIDs.
Writable-share save drops `prunedCids` without calling unpin — confirming there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path and the ownership gap is purely a security bug, not an intentional design.

Enforced journal-fsync-before-ack ordering in `handle_release`: journal.put(844) → handle.cleanup(892) → reply.ok(894) → spawn publish(904) → journal.remove on success(943). This ensures FUSE does not acknowledge a write to the kernel before the journal entry is fsynced.

`handle_mkdir` journals the MkdirPublish op at line 534 (inside the closure, before reply.entry at line 655). On conflict, sends `FsEvent::MkdirConflict` to re-arm the publisher instead of warn-only. Journal entry cleared only on parent-publish success.

Added local `IPFS_PROVIDER` useFactory to vault.module.ts to provide the IPFS provider without importing IpfsModule — the established pattern in this codebase for breaking circular NestJS module dependencies.

workflow: GSD wave-based execution pattern: isolate each plan executor in a git worktree off a captured base SHA, collect results asynchronously via task notifications, merge worktrees back via cleanup-wave manifest, then run post-merge build+test gates before advancing.

Migration blocking checkpoint (human-verify gate) auto-approved under `--auto` only after independent orchestrator verification — the orchestrator ran `to_regclass()` directly against the live DB rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported result.

Code review is advisory only in the GSD pipeline — it must always run (never skipped) but its findings never block phase completion. On missing SECURITY.md, flag `/gsd:secure-phase N` in next-steps output rather than blocking.

When a planner agent dies mid-run (socket error), recover by: (1) verifying which plan files landed on disk with complete frontmatter, (2) spawning a continuation planner scoped to the missing plans only.
For git commits in subagents under 1Password signing: always use `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`; never use `--no-gpg-sign`; on signing failure ask user to restart 1Password before retrying.

Phase branch topology: each phase gets a dedicated `feat/<phase-slug>` branch. When planning phase N+1 after completing phase N, rebase the N+1 branch onto the completed N branch before spawning executors so context files are visible.
Worktree merge conflicts (e.g., 42-05) can leave `MERGE_HEAD` in place after auto-resolution; conclude with explicit `git commit --no-edit` rather than re-running cleanup-wave.
Always answer user questions directly in prose first before presenting options menus — presenting the menu without answering the question is perceived as evasive and unhelpful.

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures mid-execution required user to restart the app and retry with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` — interrupted the planning flow and required a manual recovery step.
gsd commit helper false negatives (`committed: false` while commit actually landed) caused repeated unnecessary retry attempts and `git log` verification overhead on every commit.
cleanup-wave not idempotent: once an entry is merged, rerunning the same manifest causes `branch_mismatch` and aborts, requiring manual manifest surgery to remove already-processed entries.
cleanup-wave cwd sensitivity: running it from inside a worktree instead of repo root silently produces wrong `base_mismatch` errors with no actionable message.
42-05 merge left MERGE_HEAD in an unfinished state after auto-resolution, requiring a manual `git commit --no-edit` and worktree/branch cleanup.

`nest build` side-effect writes formatting-only changes to `openapi.json` in the main worktree, causing spurious merge conflicts when any Wave 3 executor also regenerated it — required `git checkout --` restore before merge.
prettier mangled VALIDATION.md regex pipe characters (`|`) into table columns, breaking the test command in a way that wasn't caught until the planner agent's output was reviewed.
Planner agent socket error mid-run (after writing 3 of 8 plans) required manual filesystem recovery and a continuation spawn — no graceful checkpoint/resume mechanism.
pnpm jest flag passthrough (`--filter pkg test -- --testPathPattern`) silently produces wrong test runs rather than failing loudly — caused confusion about which tests were actually running.
Session context limit hit during code-review dispatch of phase 42, requiring full context reconstruction from summary on resume.
User sent accidental text input ('touring wyatt web bossy') twice during active execution, requiring tool rejection and recovery acknowledgment.
